description: Frontend live-log resilience (LLR-5, LLR-6). LLR-5: automatic viewer reconnection for unexpected aggregate-WS drops using bounded exponential backoff, distinguishing intentional closes (sources change, new Search, switch to History, close workspace, unmount) from unexpected drops, showing a 'reconnecting' state, resuming current Live params on success, and falling back to the terminal error state on exhaustion without an infinite loop — respecting Pause and not duplicating/reordering rendered lines. LLR-6: map a 502/connection-refused failure class to a distinguished, actionable, secret-free 'backend unavailable' message in api.ts and PodDetailsPanel.tsx (presentation-only, no REST contract change). Frontend-only. Depends on FEAT-001 only in that LLR-1 keeps the backend alive to reconnect to; the code changes here are independent and can be implemented against the existing backend.
steps: Read context.json and this file FIRST. Run `npm install` once at the worktree root if node_modules is absent. Note: the frontend test runner is `tsx --test src/**/*.test.ts` and runs .test.ts ONLY with NO DOM/React harness — put all testable logic in pure modules and test those; do NOT add test libraries.

LLR-5 policy module: Create frontend/src/logsReconnect.ts as a pure module exposing createReconnectPolicy({ baseMs=500, factor=2, maxDelayMs=10000, maxAttempts=6 }) -> { nextDelay(): number | null, reset(): void, attempts: number } where null means exhausted, plus a classifier for intentional vs unexpected close given an intentionalClose flag. Add frontend/src/logsReconnect.test.ts covering backoff growth, cap at maxDelayMs, exhaustion returns null, and reset restoring attempts, following the node:test + node:assert/strict pattern in frontend/src/logsLiveSession.test.ts.
LLR-5 state label: Add a 'reconnecting' member to LogConnectionState in frontend/src/components/LogViewerParts.tsx and give it a stateLabel entry.

LLR-5 wiring: In frontend/src/components/LogViewer.tsx add an intentionalCloseRef set true before every user-initiated teardown (sources change, new Search, switch to History, onClose/close workspace, and the session effect cleanup/unmount). In the LIVE branch only (applied.mode === 'live'), when socket.onclose/onerror fires with the flag false and the session is not already terminal, set connection state 'reconnecting' and schedule a reopen using the policy; on successful reopen reset the policy; on exhaustion set 'error' with the existing message ('Could not connect to the aggregate log stream.'). Respect pausedRef (no auto-scroll/duplicate) and reuse the existing dedup/append + CLIENT_LOG_BUFFER cap (reconnect the session, NOT byte-exact resume). Leave the history/query socket error/close handling unchanged.

LLR-6: In frontend/src/api.ts add an exported backendUnavailableMessage() and make errorFrom return a distinguished error for HTTP 502; also classify fetch rejections / connection-refused as backend-unavailable (shared helper or per-caller) carrying a marker (e.g. a BackendUnavailableError subclass or an error with kind:'backend-unavailable'). In frontend/src/components/PodDetailsPanel.tsx messageOf, present the distinguished actionable, secret-free message instead of raw 'HTTP 502'. Presentation-only; do not change any REST call shape, path, or status handling elsewhere.

LLR-6 tests: Add frontend/src/api.test.ts (or extend an existing frontend test) asserting a 502 Response and a thrown network error both resolve to the distinguished backend-unavailable message, and a normal application error (e.g. JSON { error } body) still surfaces its own message, not the backend-unavailable text.

Run the FEAT-002 verification commands below; set this FEAT status to completed and record in findings any limitation (notably: the LogViewer reconnect UI wiring itself is validated by typecheck+build + the pure policy module, since there is no DOM test harness). Commit locally on branch feature/live-logs-resilience; never push.
acceptance_criteria: frontend/src/logsReconnect.ts exists as a pure module with bounded exponential backoff (base 500ms, factor 2, max delay 10s, max attempts 6) and exhaustion returns null; frontend/src/logsReconnect.test.ts passes.

LogViewer enters a 'reconnecting' state and retries on unexpected LIVE drops, resumes current Live params on success, does NOT reconnect on intentional closes, and falls back to the terminal error state on exhaustion without looping; Pause is respected and the render buffer is not corrupted.

A 502/connection-refused failure maps to a distinguished actionable, secret-free message in both api.ts and PodDetailsPanel.tsx, while application-level errors keep their own messages; no REST contract/status change.
`npm test --workspace=frontend` passes including new tests; `npm run typecheck` clean; `npm run build` succeeds.
findings:
All frontend LLR-5 + LLR-6 implemented. Frontend suite 171 tests pass (was 161; +10 new across logsReconnect.test.ts and api.test.ts); typecheck clean, build succeeds, diff --check clean. No test libraries added; no backend files touched; no REST contract/status change.

LLR-5 (auto-reconnect):
- NEW frontend/src/logsReconnect.ts — pure module. createReconnectPolicy({ baseMs=500, factor=2, maxDelayMs=10000, maxAttempts=6 }) -> { nextDelay(): number|null, reset(), attempts }. nextDelay returns Math.min(base*factor^attempts, maxDelayMs) and advances the counter; returns null once attempts reach maxAttempts (exhaustion). shouldReconnect({ intentionalClose, terminal }) is the classifier (reconnect only on an unexpected, non-terminal drop). DEFAULT_RECONNECT_CONFIG exported. NEW logsReconnect.test.ts covers growth, cap, exhaustion->null, reset, default-bound schedule, and the classifier.
- frontend/src/components/LogViewerParts.tsx: added 'reconnecting' to the LogConnectionState union and a stateLabel('reconnecting') => 'reconnecting' entry.
- frontend/src/components/LogViewer.tsx WIRING (DOM-untested; see limitation below): added stateRef (synced to state), reconnectAttempt state, prevReconnectAttemptRef, intentionalCloseRef, reconnectPolicyRef, reconnectTimerRef, and module-level liveStateIsTerminal() ('ended'|'error' are terminal; 'partial' stays reconnectable, true completion is the summary reason). The existing session useEffect gained reconnectAttempt in its deps. A reconnect re-run is detected via reconnectAttempt !== prevReconnectAttemptRef (NOT a surviving ref across cleanup), and ONLY on that run are rendered Live lines preserved (eventsRef kept, events/history NOT cleared); any other dep change is a fresh session and resets the policy. socket.onopen (live) resets the policy on a successful (re)open. In the LIVE branch of socket.onerror/onclose, scheduleLiveReconnect() runs BEFORE the old error/ended handling: it no-ops for history mode, when shouldReconnect is false (intentionalClose or terminal), or when nextDelay()===null (then falls through to the existing 'error' + message 'Could not connect to the aggregate log stream.' — no infinite loop); otherwise it sets state 'reconnecting' and setTimeout(delay) -> setReconnectAttempt(+1) to re-run the effect against the current (unchanged) applied Live params. intentionalCloseRef is set true in the effect cleanup (covers sources change, new Search, History switch, onClose/close workspace, and unmount — all go through cleanup) and reset false right before each new WebSocket; a separate unmount-only effect and the cleanup both clear any pending reconnect timer. Pause is respected because reconnect reuses the existing liveSessionController/reduceLiveLogEvent path (pausedRef, dedup/append, CLIENT_LOG_BUFFER cap) unchanged. History/query socket error/close handling is unchanged (scheduleLiveReconnect returns false for history mode and runs only after the failPendingWindows/failPendingQueryWindows short-circuits).

LLR-6 (backend-unavailable messaging) — presentation only:
- frontend/src/api.ts: exported backendUnavailableMessage() (actionable, secret-free), class BackendUnavailableError extends Error with readonly kind:'backend-unavailable', and isBackendUnavailable(reason) (true for BackendUnavailableError and for TypeError = a fetch rejection / connection-refused to the local backend). errorFrom() now returns a BackendUnavailableError for HTTP 502 before attempting to parse a body; all other statuses/JSON { error } bodies are unchanged. No REST call shape/path/status handling changed elsewhere.
- frontend/src/components/PodDetailsPanel.tsx: messageOf() now returns backendUnavailableMessage() when isBackendUnavailable(reason), else the prior behavior (reason.message / 'Failed to load.').
- NEW frontend/src/api.test.ts: asserts a 502-derived BackendUnavailableError and a thrown TypeError both map to backendUnavailableMessage(), a normal application Error keeps its own message, and the message is actionable + secret-free (no authorization/token/secret/bearer/cert, not 'HTTP 502'). It mirrors PodDetailsPanel's messageOf locally since there is no DOM harness.

LIMITATION FOR REVIEWER: the LogViewer reconnect UI wiring itself (useEffect/socket lifecycle, state transitions, timer scheduling) is NOT covered by a runtime/DOM test — the frontend runner is `tsx --test src/**/*.test.ts`, .test.ts only, no React/DOM harness. That wiring is validated by typecheck + build plus the pure logsReconnect policy module tests; the backoff/classifier logic and the LLR-6 message mapping are unit-tested in pure modules. Likewise PodDetailsPanel.messageOf is covered indirectly via the mirrored helper in api.test.ts, not a component render.
